hook: Alex Zhavoronkov founded Insilico Medicine in 2014 to apply deep learning and generative models to drug discovery and aging research. The company's lead program, the TNIK inhibitor rentosertib for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, went from a nominated preclinical candidate in 2021 to positive Phase IIa results in 2024. He chairs Insilico's board and leads it as CEO, with Feng Ren serving as co-CEO, and he has written widely on longevity science.

quick_facts: Founded Insilico Medicine in 2014 and, according to the company's leadership page retrieved in October 2026, is its chairman and CEO, with Feng Ren as co-CEO.

Born in Riga, Latvia, he holds two bachelor's degrees from Queen's University in Canada (2001), a master's in biotechnology from Johns Hopkins University (2007) and a PhD in physics and mathematics from Moscow State University (2008).
Insilico's governance page credits him with more than 300 research papers and three books, among them The Ageless Generation.
Insilico moved its headquarters to Cambridge, Massachusetts, in 2024 and lists further offices in Hong Kong, Abu Dhabi and Shanghai.
Insilico's leadership page lists him as a Clarivate highly cited scientist for 2022.
Earlier roles listed in Insilico's governance filings include Deep Longevity, from 2020 to 2023, and the Biogerontology Research Foundation, from 2008 to 2018.

achievements.title: Founding Insilico Medicine (2014)
achievements.impact: Built a company that runs target discovery and molecule design through its own AI platform, and that now reports a presence in the United States, Greater China, Canada and the Middle East.

achievements.title: The rentosertib program
achievements.impact: Insilico reports that its Pharma.AI platform identified TNIK as an anti-fibrotic target and produced rentosertib. The program moved from preclinical nomination in February 2021 to a Phase 0 study in Australia that November, first Phase II dosing in June 2023 and positive Phase IIa topline results in November 2024. The drug received its USAN generic name in March 2025.

achievements.title: GENTRL in Nature Biotechnology (2019)
achievements.impact: As first author, described generative tensorial reinforcement learning, a deep generative model for designing small molecules, and used it to find inhibitors of the DDR1 kinase.

achievements.title: Writing on longevity
achievements.impact: Wrote The Ageless Generation (2013) on how advances in biomedicine could change the global economy, and has continued to publish on aging research alongside his drug discovery work.
